question.text: Under the Companies Act, 2013, Section 31 deals with shelf prospectus. For how long is a shelf prospectus valid from the date of opening of the first offer of securities under it?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 31 of the Companies Act, 2013, a shelf prospectus is valid for up to 1 year, with the validity period commencing from the date of opening of the first offer of securities under it. During this period, no further prospectus is required for the 2nd or subsequent offers — only an information memorandum needs to be filed for any material changes. The Trap: "2 years" and "3 years" may seem logical for a shelf document, but the law limits validity to 1 year to ensure investors receive reasonably current information. Note: The validity clock starts from the date the first offer opens under the shelf prospectus, not from the date the prospectus is first filed or issued.
